title: Can local LLMs be used for vibe coding in game development?
author: Danilo_____
selftext:
I have an RTX 4090 with 24 GB of VRAM, and I’m wondering if there are already any local LLMs advanced enough to be useful for vibe coding.


I know we’re not at the point where we have anything equivalent to Fable or Astra yet, but are there any good local alternatives that could help reduce token costs during development?

comments.author: theartofennui
comments.body: i have a 4090, you can load qwen3.8-27b with a limited context and ultimately that's where it falls apart. you can probably vibe code a basic retro style game but that's about as far as it'll go

replies.author: Serious_Bite_7613
replies.body: Nah you can load a moderately quantised version at full context.

replies.author: machyume
replies.body: This. I have this running right now on my MacBook M3. It is surprisingly fast.

replies.author: Excellent-Basket-825
replies.body: Naw man look into nninfer for 4090 209k context

replies.author: Aztec_Man
replies.body:
qwen3.8-27b is a dense model. The mixture-of-experts models run faster due to loading a subset of the weights during inference. Check out Qwen3.8-Flash-Next... I bet it will be an improvement. It's also shown some increase on the benchmarks over the dense model.  
[https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next)

comments.author: SeasonNo3107
comments.body: Dual 3090s and get 262k context with like 50-70tps. Gotta be smart about context and prompting. Smarter than I am but my app has every feature i have thought of so far and it's like 5,000 lines of code at 60k context just for the application. Edits can take up 100k context per prompt with skills and map for something I'd consider a small change but I cannot change myself and is actually a big change. Make a change, summarize it, start new chat in the same project to do more stuff. It's a media app though not a game. If you were really clever you could make a great simple game and thats what people like most sometimes. But it's not a powerhouse to throw anything at, you have to be economical and fail a prompt 4 or 5 times (I'm not a coder) before giving the small intelligence a poorly structured task. I do less of this prompting with opencode and unsloth studio because it's an agent but I HAVE to put the agent in a plan first or it blows context solving problems I could have easily avoided by prompting a bit better. If you're not lazy with creativity and learning you can do amazing things you never could before. As LLM progress, your skills learned doing this will magnify when using a better model

comments.author: Kooky_Technology_782
comments.body: I have a laptop 5090 with 24gb VRAM and spent quite a bit of time trying to make Qwen 27b useful in Unity development. I eventually just tapped out and used Deepseek. I don’t think I’d even bother trying again with less than 64gb. You have so many dirt cheap cloud providers that it makes it anti-productive to try it locally when this constrained.

replies.author: No_Advance3911
replies.body: I can't figure out how exactly you used Qwen locally to get nothing working? I'm currently running on 16GB VRAM and getting great results in Unity and other engines. I'm using local Qwen for development on pretty much every project I'm working on right now and haven't run into any issues. What kind of tasks are you giving the model? Something like "Make me an AAA game?"???

comments.author: vlad_h
comments.body: They can with some limitations. Check out my repo on GitHub for a local setup. The-Running-Dev/SubZeroDev.Workspace

comments.author: owenwp
comments.body:
Sure, you can, but you probably shouldn't. Whatever you save in API cost you will pay for many times over in wasted time as the smaller models fail to handle large tasks repeatedly. You will also hit a complexity limit as you develop your project where the small models fail to attend to enough information to make meaningful edits without breaking old code. 

Also these models are still not actually free to use, running your GPU at max power for around 200 hours will cost around the same as a month of GPT plus subscription, and you will need a lot of hours to iterate until your coding tasks succeed.

comments.author: FrenchLiviela
comments.body:
In time, but not now. Even Astra isn't perfect yet. 

If you want cheap, wait. Even just 1 year of progress for any of the models is huge, and it will trickle down to local models if things go right. If you can be patient, you can quickly build a better product from scratch a few years from now instead of patching up imperfect projects with a broken foundation.

comments.author: Nomski88
comments.body: Yes 100%. I'm working on a quake inspired 3d engine that introduces new features from other games like hl2 etc. It's a fully functioning 3d engine built from scratch using qwen3.8 27b and my 5090. I used ChatGPT to plant the master project prompt as well as breakdown the project into phase and help with troubleshooting etc. I'm about one week into the project and have a fully playable 3d core engine that loads quake levels and fully navigate them with collisions, physics, jumping crouching etc. I'm in the middle of Phase 7 where I'm implementing moving doors, platforms, buttons etc. All done in C++ and OpenGl/SDL.
